description: Defines permitted and prohibited platform statements per evidence class (observed feature, reference comparison, diagnostic inference, feedback recommendation, longitudinal evidence, learning outcome) with machine-checkable banned-vocabulary guardrails.
scope: all platform statements about learners or corpus-derived evidence

statements.statement: Observed feature statements may state value, unit, version, and evidence location; they may not judge the learner.
Reference comparison statements must carry group, versions, effective N, availability, and fallback disclosure; normative interpretation is blocked.
The learner has advanced proficiency, the learner mastered this skill, and the learner improved are prohibited from corpus descriptive evidence.
Diagnostic inference statements require gate version, evidence ids, and prototype limitation wording; they may not assert learner traits.
Feedback recommendations carry evidence and provenance; practice completion is activity completion only.
Mastery, learning, or ability claims attached to practice completion or feedback are prohibited.
Longitudinal output must be descriptive with HISTORY_LIMITATION wording; improvement/decline/mastery/regression claims are prohibited.
Learning outcome statements are reserved for validated measurement models behind the outcome-layer gate; none may be made today.
Banned vocabulary (level, score, ability, mastery, gain, cefr; word boundary) must not appear in corpus-derived field names or UI strings.
Risky ability phrases (advanced proficiency, mastery, native-like, superior writing ability, etc.) are prohibited in learner-directed statements.
Display may downgrade epistemic layers, never upgrade them.
L2 diagnostic evidence and Academic research evidence never share a schema or claim templates.
Direct learner-to-learner comparison statements (e.g., outperforms peers) are prohibited.
